title: Equations of motion
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the constant-acceleration equations of motion; uniform circular motion and projectile motion are different ideas, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Equations of motion
card: The equations apply only when acceleration is constant along a straight line. The symbols are u (initial velocity), v (final velocity), a (acceleration), t (time) and s (displacement).
v = u + at links final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time. It has no s in it.
s = ut + ½at² links displacement, initial velocity, acceleration and time. It has no v in it.
Pick the equation that holds the three quantities you know and the one you want. Take one direction as positive and give signs to match.
draft.remember: Constant acceleration only. Choose the equation that leaves out the quantity you do not need.

a.q: A trolley starts from rest and accelerates at 3 m/s² for 4 s. What is its final velocity?
a.why: Use v = u + at, so v = 0 + 3 × 4 = 12 m/s. Adding 3 and 4 to get 7 mixes up the quantities, as acceleration is multiplied by time.

b.q: A car moving at 10 m/s accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. How far does it travel in this time?
b.why: Use s = ut + ½at²: s = 10 × 5 + ½ × 2 × 25 = 50 + 25 = 75 m. Giving 50 m leaves out the extra distance gained from accelerating.
b.clue: You need the equation with s, u, a and t, and no v.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: v = 0 + 3 × 4 = 12 m/s, and s = 10 × 5 + ½ × 2 × 5² = 75 m.
